why: Grid path costs with an extra state: which grid you are on. best[g][r][c] is the cheapest arrival at (r, c) on grid g; after entering a cell you may switch layers once for switchCost.
hints: The usual min-path DP forgets which grid you are on. Add that as a third index.
Arriving at (r, c) on grid k costs grid_k[r][c] + min(best[k] above, best[k] left). Then allow a switch at the cell: best[0] = min(best[0], best[1] + switchCost) and vice versa.
Process cells row by row with two rolling rows (one per grid). Answer min(best[0], best[1]) at the bottom-right. O(rows * cols).
pitfalls: Switching does not add the cell value again.
You may start on either grid (or switch at the start cell).
Do the switch relaxation after computing both arrivals for the cell.
